title: Lakeland man ordained deacon after journey from addiction to recovery
text:
Lakeland man ordained deacon after journey from addiction to recovery
John Quirk III, the youngest of six children and only son in his family, was ordained a deacon for the Diocese of Orlando on June 6, 2026. Quirk's path to ordination included struggles with addiction, time in jail, and eventual recovery through faith and support from Narcotics Anonymous.
Quirk grew up in Lakeland in a Protestant household where his father served as a Baptist deacon. Despite active participation in church activities during his youth, he recalled feelings of guilt and not belonging. In high school, Quirk began using drugs after being introduced by his sister’s boyfriend. "I fell in love — from the first time with drugs, the feeling, the escape," he said.
After graduating near the top of his class despite substance abuse issues, Quirk joined the Navy but continued using drugs until he was caught and court-martialed during Desert Storm. Returning home led to further struggles until an arrest placed him before a drug court program that offered treatment instead of prison if he could stay clean. A paperwork error delayed his enrollment; another arrest threatened him with a long sentence.
In jail on his 24th birthday, Quirk said he prayed, "God, I’m not going to bargain with you anymore because I don’t deserve it... Please don’t let me use anymore. Please forgive me." He described feeling relief after this prayer: "I immediately felt like the weight of the world was lifted off my back." Eventually released into his parents’ custody under strict conditions including daily attendance at Narcotics Anonymous meetings, Quirk began rebuilding his life through recovery programs and renewed faith.
Quirk’s journey included work as a social worker for troubled teens and growing involvement with church communities across several states. After marrying Enidza—who is Catholic—and experiencing what he called a spiritual awakening at their son's birth, Quirk entered Catholic formation through OCIA and became active at St. Joseph’s parish in Lakeland as well as service organizations like Knights of Columbus.
With encouragement from clergy such as Father Tim LaBo and support from family despite concerns about his past history disqualifying him for ministry roles, Quirk completed diaconate formation over several years before ordination. Today he says feelings of unworthiness are behind him: “If He can love me, He can love anybody.”
The Diocese of Orlando was established in 1968 and includes Brevard, Lake, Marion, Orange, Osceola, Polk, Seminole, Sumter, and Volusia counties; it currently comprises 79 parishes along with schools and missions under Bishop James Noonan’s leadership,according to The Diocese of Orlando.
